answers:
1. I don't have a voicemail callback rate or weekly hours for the old calling. What I do know is that front desk staff now save about 11 hours a week on confirmation calls, and honestly I think that's the bigger win.

2. I can't describe the exact text screen word for word, but the key thing is patients can reply to reschedule, and that two-way texting is what really drove the drop, not the reminders themselves. One thing it showed us: some older patients reply "OK" and still don't show up.

3. The 11 hours a week saved on confirmation calls is the real number I have. I don't have appointments recovered or per-clinic hours. The Gdańsk clinic is a good moment, though. Joanna, our front desk lead there, noticed the elderly patients replying "OK" but not coming, so now staff also phone every patient over 70.

4. Sopot only got down to 12% and nobody's sure why. The "OK" replies from older patients not turning up surprised us too. I don't know if the drop was steady or in steps, and I worry the six months included summer, when no-shows usually dip anyway.

5. Not really. I'd tell a colleague the two-way part, letting patients reschedule by replying, is what mattered, and that texts alone don't cover everyone, so we still call patients over 70. The system costs $1,400 a month across all clinics, which I'm fine sharing. I can't name the vendor, because our contract forbids it without approval.
reply2:
I built this from your answers and kept your phrasing where I could. Three things to know:

- The vendor stays unnamed, and I kept a short line saying why.
- Your summer worry is in the post as a caveat. It's the kind of detail readers trust.
- I cut the "meeting people where they already are" lesson and the closing question, since you said that wasn't really your takeaway.

<final>
We cut no-shows at Brightwell Dental Group from 18% to 7% in six months. Some of that may be summer, when no-shows usually dip anyway, and I don't know whether the drop was steady or came in steps.

We switched to text message reminders across all 9 of our clinics. The system costs $1,400 a month for all of them. I can't name the vendor because our contract forbids it without approval.

Phone calls were hit or miss. Front desk teams left voicemails that rarely got returned. What changed things was two-way texting. Patients can reply to reschedule, and I think that did more than the reminders themselves.

The bigger win, I think, is that front desk staff now save about 11 hours a week on confirmation calls.

Texts don't cover everyone. Joanna, our front desk lead in Gdańsk, noticed that some older patients reply "OK" and still don't show up. Now staff also phone every patient over 70. Sopot only got down to 12%, and nobody is sure why.

If you run a multi-location practice and still rely on calls, it's worth testing. Make sure patients can reply to reschedule, and expect to keep calling some of them.
</final>
